Class SlotWindowResolver

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.window.SlotWindowResolver
@Internal public final class SlotWindowResolver extends Object
Resolves an Address back to its live backing — the resolution mechanics of THE ONE WINDOW (still no behavior; pure location). Given the live screen, it answers "what slot is this address, right now?" and "where is it on screen?".

The held-handle no-op (Lead condition #3a) is structural here

Every resolution first checks that the address's root owner matches what WindowMint derives from the LIVE menu. A handle used on the wrong (or no) screen fails this check and resolves to Optional.empty() — one guard, identical for every kind, no per-call-site screen test. (Writes drop at the engine layer for the same reason; that lands with Phase 3.)

Tiering

Vanilla-slot resolution is pure MK (a menu-space index lookup) and works with MK alone. Created-slot resolution delegates to the CreatedSlotResolver port (MKC) — null when MKC is absent, so created slots simply don't resolve client-only. Panel/element resolution arrives with the handle (Phase 6, via the panel registry).

This class is built but not yet CALLED — the minting/calling sites are the handle (Phase 6) and the engine (Phase 3). Verified here by compile + review; exercised live once the handle wires it.

Internal plumbing. Address→live-Slot resolution is an engine concern; consumers address everything by Address and never receive a raw vanilla Slot from this layer. Only MK/MKC's own resolution and created-slot port wiring call here.

      public static Optional<net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot> resolve(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen, Address address)
      The live in-menu Slot an address names on this screen, or empty if the address doesn't belong to this screen (held-handle no-op) or names nothing present. Returns the slot AS IT SITS IN menu.slots (the creative wrapper on creative), so a click routes correctly.

    • resolvePosition

      public static Optional<SlotScreenRect> resolvePosition(net.minecraft.client.gui.screens.inventory.AbstractContainerScreen<?> screen, Address address)
      The absolute on-screen item box for an address, or empty (same no-op rules). Vanilla slots report their in-menu x/y (the creative wrapper carries creative coords); created slots report their renderX/renderY via the port; both are offset by the live screen frame.
